extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review paper critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. The paper discusses limitations of current datasets, reviews existing algorithms, and discusses future directions for VQA and image understanding research.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan, Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science, Rochester Institute of Technology
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Multiple VQA datasets are reviewed. Data collection methods vary by dataset: DAQUAR uses images from NYU-DepthV2; COCO-QA uses NLP algorithms to derive QA pairs from COCO captions; COCO-VQA uses Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and answers; Visual Genome uses both free-form and region-specific annotation methods; FM-IQA was originally collected in Chinese with human-generated questions and answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from NYU-DepthV2 (DAQUAR), Microsoft COCO dataset (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W), YFCC100M/Flickr100M and COCO (Visual Genome), and synthetic cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For COCO-QA, longer sentences are broken into smaller chunks for ease of processing by the NLP algorithm. For COCO-VQA multiple-choice format, choices include the correct answer, plausible answers collected without seeing the image, popular answers, and randomly selected correct answers for other questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation methods vary by dataset. COCO-VQA: AMT workers asked to 'Stump a smart robot' for question generation; separate workers generated answers; 10 independent annotators per question. Visual Genome: free-form questions and region-specific questions prompted by bounding-box annotations. DAQUAR-consensus: average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question. FM-IQA: human-generated questions and answers, originally in Chinese.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is about 83.3% using AccuracyVQA. Over 13% of yes/no answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. For 'Why' questions, over 59% have less than three annotators giving exactly the same answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question for COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA; average of 5 for DAQUAR-consensus; average of 17 QA pairs per image for Visual Genome
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used for COCO-QA to derive QA pairs from image captions
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA could aid blind and visually impaired individuals by enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing VQA datasets contain strong language biases. In COCO-VQA, 'yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions, and almost 59% are answered with 'yes'. Question-only models can achieve 49.6% accuracy on COCO-VQA. Datasets also contain biases in question types, with easier questions (object recognition) being more frequent than harder ones (Why/Where questions).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small and contains exclusively indoor scenes. COCO-QA has grammatical errors and only four question types. COCO-VQA contains subjective questions, language biases, and inflated scores due to evaluation metric issues. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution makes evaluation challenging. Current datasets are insufficient to evaluate whether an algorithm has 'solved' VQA.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of VQA algorithms. Also used for benchmarking image understanding systems. Potential applications include aiding blind and visually impaired individuals, improving human-computer interaction, and image retrieval.

name.evidence: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges

description.evidence: In this review, we critically examine the current state of VQA in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. In particular, we discuss the limitations of current datasets with regard to their ability to properly train and assess VQA algorithms. We then exhaustively review existing algorithms for VQA.

creator.evidence: Kushal Kae and Christopher Kanan, Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science, Rochester Institute of Technology, Rochester, NY, 14623, USA

inLanguage.evidence: The dataset was originally collected in Chinese, but English translations have been made available.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: COCO-VQA consists of three questions per image, with ten answers per question. Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image... In COCO-QA, QA pairs are created for images using an Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithm that derives them from the COCO image captions.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: With exception of DAQUAR, all of the datasets include images from the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset, which consists of 328,000 images, 91 common object categories with over 2 million labeled instances, and an average of 5 captions per image. Visual Genome and Visual7W use images from Flickr100M in addition to the COCO images.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Since the release of the first VQA dataset in 2014, additional datasets have been released and many algorithms have been proposed.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Longer sentences are broken into smaller chunks for ease of processing, but in many of these cases the algorithm does not cope well with the presence of clauses and grammatical variations in sentence formation.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions... Each of the questions is then answered by 10 independent annotators.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Using AccuracyVQA, the inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is only 83.3%. It is impossible for an algorithm to achieve 100% accuracy. Inter-human agreement is especially poor for 'Why' questions, with over 59% of these questions having less than three annotators giving exactly the same answer.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: COCO-VQA consists of three questions per image, with ten answers per question... For DAQUAR-consensus, an average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question were collected... Visual Genome contains 1.7 million QA pairs for images, with an average of 17 QA pairs per image.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: In COCO-QA, QA pairs are created for images using an Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithm that derives them from the COCO image captions.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The most immediate is as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images both on the web and in the real world. For example, as a blind user scrolls through their social media feed, a captioning system can describe the image and then the user could use VQA to query the image to get more insight about the scene.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Relatively simple image-blind algorithms have achieved 49.6% accuracy on COCO-VQA using the question alone. ...`yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions, and almost 59% of them are answered with `yes.'

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While DAQUAR was a pioneering dataset for VQA, it is too small to successfully train and evaluate more complex models. Apart from the small size, DAQUAR contains exclusively indoor scenes... Existing VQA benchmarks are not sufficient to evaluate whether an algorithm has 'solved' VQA.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: These datasets enable VQA systems to be trained and evaluated... The most immediate is as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals... More generally, VQA could be used to improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content. A VQA system can also be used for image retrieval, without using image meta-data or tags.
